definitions.explanation: A genre of fiction or thought that imagines scientific and technological developments beyond current reality, or the speculative science depicted in such works.

examples.japanese: {空想|くうそう}{科学|かがく}{小説|しょうせつ}が{好|す}きだ。
かつての{空想|くうそう}{科学|かがく}が{現実|げんじつ}になった{例|れい}は{多|おお}い。
examples.english: There are many examples of what was once science fiction becoming reality.

examples.japanese: {空想|くうそう}{科学|かがく}の{世界|せかい}では{人類|じんるい}が{宇宙|うちゅう}を{自由|じゆう}に{旅|たび}する。
examples.english: In the world of science fiction, humanity travels freely through space.

notes:
A compound of {空想|くうそう} (fantasy; imagination) and {科学|かがく} (science). Used as a more traditional Japanese term for the science fiction genre. The popular book series {空想|くうそう}{科学|かがく}{読本|どくほん} (by Yanagita Rikao) humorously analyzes the scientific plausibility of anime and manga, making this term widely recognized.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {空想|くうそう}{科学|かがく}{小説|しょうせつ}: science fiction novel
- {空想|くうそう}{科学|かがく}{映画|えいが}: science fiction film
- {空想|くうそう}{科学|かがく}{読本|どくほん}: science fiction reader (famous book series)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- SF（エスエフ）: science fiction — the most common abbreviation used in Japanese
- サイエンスフィクション: science fiction — the full loanword, less commonly used
- {空想|くうそう}: fantasy; daydream — the broader concept of imagining things that don't exist
